$Comment: Standalone-rich by design: this station is fully useful on its own (a classic direct convert loop - place raw fish, press use, get grilled fish) and doubles as the multi-station anchor the cutting board's PrepFish program claims by proximity and type (Anchors:{fire:{Station:'cookingfire',...}} on Actions/PrepFish.json). When claimed as a remote anchor, this station's own action is never invoked; only its Custody claim (the anchor's own placed-input slot) and its block's State.Definitions (Default/Loaded/Lit) matter, and the claiming program's own Steps execute at this anchor with the fire's presentation. Custody.States carries a nullable Working leaf ('Lit = actively cooking'): the burning look lives on Working, so Loaded is a distinct non-burning has-fish state - placing raw fish on a cold fire leaves it dark until a cook/convert step actually starts running here, and it darkens again on finish/stop/abort/ANCHOR_LOST/PATH_BLOCKED/INPUTS_EXHAUSTED and across the fish program's walk phases. Both routes share one engine seam: this station's own plain-F convert loop (the implicit Consume+Produce step is a convert, so it lights from engage - the whole 2500ms CycleMs is the cook time) and the cutting board's PrepFish program lighting this block as its claimed 'fire' anchor (its cook step authors Working:true explicitly, since a pure Duration beat is not a convert). Presentation.Sound SFX_Flame_Ignite is the per-cook sizzle beat (a real vanilla one-shot, Sounds/Items/Torch/Torch_On.ogg - deliberately not a looping event, since nothing in the protocol can stop a looping sound once played); the crackle loop and the embers live natively on the block's own Lit state instead. A Puppet group is authored here for this station's own direct cook loop, modelled on the sawmill's shipped defaults (Enabled true, Hide.Route 'Scale', Look.Source 'PlayerClone', Prop MirrorHeld/Hotbar); only the placement leaves differ, for a low campfire block rather than a waist-high bench. Offset/Yaw are facing-relative to the placed block's own yaw (authored +Z is the block's front, +X its right, Yaw 0 means 'faces the same way the block does'), so Offset.Z 0.9 puts the cook just in front of the fire at any placement orientation and Offset.Y -0.45 drops them to a crouch-height stance over a low fire. Every placement leaf here is provisional/in-game-unverified, same as the sawmill's and anvil's own values; both Offset and Yaw are plain JSON leaves, so a re-tune is a one-line edit with no code change. When this station is claimed as a remote anchor by the cutting board's PrepFish program its own action is never invoked, so this Puppet group governs only a direct press-F cook here and never competes with the cutting board's own puppet. No Animation.EmoteId is authored, so the puppet stands holding the mirrored held item rather than looping a work clip - the cook beat's presentation carries the moment instead. Custody.States.Loaded='Lit' names the block's own lit-campfire state variant (RPG_Station_CookingFire.json). Custody.Display is the flat Fish_Piece-model item prop: the placed item's own BlockType.CustomModel/CustomModelTexture renders through the item-route prop automatically (Food_Fish_Raw / Food_Fish_Grilled both model Resources/Ingredients/Fish_Piece.blockymodel with a raw-vs-roasted texture swap baked into each item), so this Display group only needs Offset/Scale, never a model reference - Offset.Y is a first-pass placeholder, provisional/in-game-unverified like every other shipped Custody.Display in this family. Recipe.FromCrafting.Benches:['Campfire'] + Types:['Processing'] document the real native Food_Fish_Grilled recipe (Input:[{ItemId:'Food_Fish_Raw'}], BenchRequirement:[{Id:'Campfire',Type:'Processing'}], TimeSeconds:2) - the native BenchRequirement here carries no Categories field at all, so the Sawmill's Categories-only derivation route cannot reach this recipe, which is exactly why Benches exists as a second derivation route. The hand-authored Conversions[] block is kept and is what runs: station.StationRecipeDeriver does derive from Benches, but the derived Campfire twin shares this same input ref (Food_Fish_Raw), so the authored-conversion-wins dedup suppresses the derived twin - the hand-authored Conversion is the effective one. NativeTime{Scale:1.0,OffsetMs:500} is the linear transform (y=Scale*TimeSeconds_ms+OffsetMs) documenting the native pacing (1.0*2000+500=2500ms, matching Work.CycleMs below byte-for-byte); because the derived twin it would bake onto is suppressed by the authored Conversion, NativeTime is currently inert (the authored Conversion carries no DurationMs, so Work.CycleMs stays the sole live cadence source). Dropping the authored Conversions[] would hand the recipe to the derived Benches conversion and let NativeTime take effect, at the same 2500ms pacing.
